requirements.requirement: Identify what produced the funds, receipt/earning dates, disposition dates and amounts previously reported. A US citizen's worldwide income generally remains within the US filing rules even while abroad.
requirements.condition: A current bank balance alone is not a tax-year income statement.
requirements.flag: Income categories, years and filings are not supplied.

requirements.requirement: Retain evidence of qualifying foreign income taxes imposed on and paid/accrued by the taxpayer; use Form 1116 unless a specific exception applies. Do not claim a credit for tax on FEIE-excluded income.
requirements.condition: Credit categories, source adjustments, timing and limitation must be computed from actual returns.
requirements.flag: Actual creditable Chinese tax is unknown.

requirements.requirement: For the exclusion, establish foreign earned income, a foreign tax home and either the applicable bona-fide-residence or 330-full-day physical-presence test; file the required return/Form 2555.
requirements.unit: full days in 12 consecutive months for physical-presence test
requirements.condition: Other test conditions and exceptions apply; physical presence alone is not the whole eligibility analysis.
requirements.flag: Work location, tax home and travel dates are unknown.

requirements.requirement: The 2026 maximum foreign earned income exclusion is USD 132,900 per qualifying person, subject to earned income, qualifying-day proration and timing rules.
requirements.unit: USD per qualifying person for tax year 2026
requirements.condition: Not an exclusion of a bank balance, investment gain, dividend, pension or all China-source money.
requirements.flag: Qualifying foreign earned income is not established.

requirements.requirement: A US person with a financial interest in or signature/other authority over foreign financial accounts files FinCEN Form 114 when aggregate foreign-account value exceeds USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year.
requirements.unit: USD aggregate maximum across reportable foreign accounts
requirements.condition: Account income need not be taxable for the reporting rule to apply; exceptions must be checked.
requirements.flag: The user's maximum aggregate value and other accounts are unknown.

requirements.requirement: File separately through FinCEN's BSA E-Filing System, generally by April 15 with automatic extension to October 15; generally retain required account records for five years from the FBAR due date.
requirements.condition: Disaster/special extensions and exceptions require separate checking; do not assume the income-tax extension governs FBAR.

requirements.requirement: If required to file an income-tax return, unmarried US-resident specified individuals report when specified foreign financial assets exceed USD 50,000 at year-end or USD 75,000 at any time; joint-filing thresholds are USD 100,000/150,000. Married filing separately uses USD 50,000/75,000 under the cited rules.
requirements.unit: USD year-end baseline; USD 75,000 any-time baseline for unmarried/MFS US residents
requirements.condition: Specified-person, asset, residence and return-filing conditions apply; this does not replace FBAR.
requirements.flag: Residence for this test, filing status and asset values are unknown.

requirements.requirement: For qualifying taxpayers living abroad who must file a return, non-joint thresholds are more than USD 200,000 at year-end or USD 300,000 at any time; joint thresholds are USD 400,000/600,000.
requirements.unit: USD year-end baseline; USD 300,000 any-time baseline for non-joint qualifying filers abroad
requirements.condition: The IRS living-abroad definition must be met; merely having a Chinese bank account does not establish it.
requirements.flag: Qualifying foreign tax home/presence is unverified.

requirements.requirement: Report on Form 3520 Part IV when aggregate gifts/bequests treated as such from a nonresident alien individual or foreign estate and related foreign persons exceed USD 100,000 in the tax year. Foreign trust distributions follow separate rules.
requirements.unit: USD aggregate per tax year, strictly more than
requirements.condition: A genuine gift/bequest is not the same as the recipient's own savings, salary or sale proceeds; entity gifts have a different threshold.
requirements.flag: No gift, inheritance or trust facts were supplied.

findings.topic: Transfer amount is not the tax calculation
findings.finding: The reviewed federal rules tax income, dispositions, specified currency gains and certain outbound US remittance funding separately. They do not justify applying one income-tax percentage to the entire amount merely because it moves from China to the US.
findings.implication: Reconstruct the original income and any later taxable events; do not label the whole balance a taxable remittance or universally tax-free.
findings.flag: No official blanket transfer-tax exemption is asserted.

findings.finding: Qualifying Chinese income tax may reduce US tax on the same income through the foreign tax credit, subject to the limitation and category/source rules. A deduction instead reduces taxable income. Taxes on FEIE-excluded income cannot also generate a credit.
findings.implication: Compare credit and exclusion using actual income and taxes; do not add the full Chinese tax and full US tax as an unavoidable combined penalty.
findings.flag: Actual credit and residual US tax remain blank.

findings.finding: Protocol paragraph 2 preserves US taxation of its citizens notwithstanding the treaty, subject to the listed exceptions. Article 22 provides credit relief under US law; the treaty is not a general election to be taxed only in China.
findings.implication: Do not claim treaty residence eliminates US citizen tax on the CNY balance or its underlying income.
findings.flag: Treaty residence and any listed exception are unverified.

findings.finding: The treaty's dividend/interest provisions contain residence and beneficial-owner conditions and a 10% source-tax limit in the cited cases. They do not establish that every US passport holder qualifies for that rate or that the US tax is eliminated.
findings.implication: Check treaty residence, domestic law and beneficial ownership before claiming a reduced rate; do not confuse this limit with a corporate-only domestic rate.
findings.flag: No treaty-claim eligibility determination is made.

findings.finding: FEIE can apply to qualifying pay for services performed abroad, not to dividends, interest, capital gains or pensions. The 2026 maximum is USD 132,900 per qualifying person, with proration and timing restrictions.
findings.implication: A salary balance may have different US treatment from investment or property proceeds; accumulated savings are not a new annual exclusion.
findings.flag: Whether any salary qualifies, and for which year, remains unverified.

findings.topic: Blocked income may matter for genuinely nonconvertible funds
findings.finding: Publication 54 permits reporting now or electing deferral for income not readily convertible because of foreign-country restrictions. It becomes unblocked when convertible or converted, and also when used for personal expenses or disposed of by gift/bequest/devise. The election requires the prescribed information return and accounting-method permissions in the stated circumstances.
findings.implication: Difficulty wiring a balance is not automatically blocked income, particularly where lawful conversion routes exist. Review prior elections before treating a later conversion as the taxable year.
findings.flag: Actual legal nonconvertibility and any prior deferral election are unknown.

findings.finding: The official 2024 Code text treats dispositions of nonfunctional currency, including bank deposits, as section 988 transactions, generally ordinary gain/loss. Section 988(e) excludes qualifying personal-transaction exchange gain only when the otherwise recognized gain does not exceed USD 200; business/investment transactions are not automatically personal.
findings.implication: Do not assume a CNY-to-USD conversion has zero US currency-gain consequences. Functional currency, basis, purpose and gain must be established. This is not a tax on the original principal by default.
findings.flag: USD 200 is a condition on the exclusion, not a tax-free allowance; current OLRC amendment verification is unresolved because its section URL was unavailable.

findings.topic: FBAR is reporting, not a balance tax
findings.finding: An account can be FBAR-reportable even if it produces no taxable income. The aggregate threshold is more than USD 10,000 at any time, not a per-transfer tax-free allowance.
findings.implication: Do not split transfers or accounts to evade reporting. Maximum values across accounts and signature authority need review.
findings.flag: Whether the user must file cannot be determined without account values/authority.

findings.finding: Form 8938 has different asset scope and residence/filing-status thresholds from FBAR. Filing one does not automatically satisfy the other; no Form 8938 is required for a year with no income-tax-return filing requirement under the cited exception.
findings.implication: Use the actual year-end and maximum values, residence test and filing status; do not substitute USD 10,000 for the FATCA thresholds.
findings.flag: Applicable threshold and reporting duty remain unverified for this user.

findings.topic: Gifts, trusts and entities are not labels for own savings
findings.finding: Foreign gift/bequest reporting generally starts above USD 100,000 for foreign individuals/estates; foreign trust transactions/ownership have separate triggers and exceptions. A transfer of the user's own money does not become a foreign gift by changing its label.
findings.implication: Do not route through relatives or a trust/company to disguise ownership. Genuine gifts, trusts, PFICs and foreign corporations require their own analysis and potentially Forms 3520, 8621 or 5471.
findings.flag: No trust/entity/gift arrangement is established; no structure is recommended.

findings.finding: The US main-home exclusion may cover up to USD 250,000 of qualifying gain, or USD 500,000 for qualifying joint filers, under US ownership/use conditions. It is separate from China's exemption and does not exclude the whole sale price.
findings.implication: If the balance arose from a home sale, compute USD gain/basis and test both countries separately; do not subtract the exclusion from the transfer principal.
findings.flag: No home sale, basis, gain or US eligibility facts were supplied.

findings.finding: NIIT may add 3.8% on the statutory lesser amount for affected investment income; FEIE does not reduce self-employment tax. China is not listed in the SSA's current totalization-agreement table.
findings.implication: Do not treat foreign income tax credits or FEIE as eliminating every US tax. Social-security/self-employment exposure depends on the actual work arrangement, not on the wire route.
findings.flag: Investment income, MAGI and employment arrangement are unknown.

findings.finding: Eligible non-willful taxpayers meeting the specified non-residency test generally submit three return years and six FBAR years with tax and interest; the official page describes relief from specified penalties, subject to its conditions and fraud/willfulness exclusions.
findings.implication: A possible compliance route if past omissions exist, not a way to avoid tax on a current transfer and not automatic amnesty.
findings.flag: No delinquency or eligibility is assumed.

findings.finding: The domestic route generally requires three amended return years, six FBAR years, tax/interest and a 5% miscellaneous offshore penalty on the defined highest aggregate value of covered foreign financial assets.
findings.implication: The 5% base is not automatically the current account balance or every foreign asset; eligibility and covered assets require professional computation.
findings.flag: Penalty amount is blank; non-willfulness and eligibility are unverified.

findings.finding: CBP requires reporting more than USD 10,000 in currency/covered monetary instruments entering or leaving the US, with family/group aggregation. The page describes a reporting mandate, not a USD 10,000 maximum lawful carrying amount.
findings.implication: If lawfully exported from China, declare correctly on US entry. Never divide family funds to evade the report; China exit rules still need independent confirmation.
findings.flag: China-side cash thresholds are not established by this US source.

findings.topic: 2026 US remittance excise is outbound from the US
findings.finding: The IRS describes a 1% tax from 2026-01-01 on specified remittances sent from the US to foreign recipients when funded with cash or similar physical instruments. That scope is not a tax on inbound China-to-US repatriation merely because the recipient is American.
findings.implication: Do not add 1% to a China-to-US wire. If later sending cash-funded money back out of the US, check the final rules and provider quote; the retrieved April 2026 regulatory details were proposed.
findings.flag: Final regulatory details beyond the official release were not verified.
